How to Descale a Breville Espresso Machine: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide

Knowing how to descale a Breville espresso machine is essential for maintaining consistent coffee quality, protecting internal components, and extending the life of your equipment. Over time, minerals naturally present in tap water accumulate inside an espresso machine, creating limescale and restricting water flow. This buildup can affect coffee extraction, brewing temperature, espresso taste, and overall machine performance.

Whether you own a Breville Barista Express, Barista Pro, Barista Touch, Bambino Plus, or Breville Oracle, regular descaling helps remove mineral deposits from the internal water system. Although the exact descaling procedure varies between models, the basic process involves preparing a suitable descaling solution, running the descaling cycle, and flushing the machine with fresh water.

This beginner-friendly guide explains how to descale different Breville espresso machine models, which descaling products to use, how often to perform maintenance, and how to troubleshoot common problems.

Why Do You Need to Descale a Breville Espresso Machine?

Descaling removes mineral deposits that accumulate inside the machine as water passes through its heating and brewing systems.

Tap water contains dissolved minerals, particularly calcium and magnesium. When water heats inside a boiler or thermocoil, these minerals can gradually form hard deposits known as limescale.

If you regularly use your Breville espresso machine without descaling it, mineral buildup can affect several important components.

Common Problems Caused by Limescale

  • Restricted water flow: Scale buildup inside water lines and internal pipes can reduce the amount of water reaching the group head.

  • Inconsistent brewing temperature: Mineral deposits around the heating element, boiler, or thermocoil can interfere with efficient heating.

  • Slow espresso flow: Calcium deposits can restrict water movement and affect coffee extraction.

  • Poor espresso taste: Mineral accumulation and inconsistent brewing conditions can contribute to unpleasant or inconsistent espresso taste.

  • Steam wand problems: Internal deposits can affect steam production and create a blocked steam wand.

  • Pump strain: Restricted internal passages can make it harder for the pump to move water through the system.

What Is the Difference Between Cleaning and Descaling?

Cleaning and descaling are two different maintenance processes. Both are necessary, but they address different types of buildup.

Maintenance task

What it removes

Main purpose

Cleaning

Coffee oils, grounds, and residue

Keeps brewing components clean

Descaling

Limescale and mineral buildup

Protects internal water systems

Water filter replacement

Helps reduce certain water impurities and minerals

Supports better water quality

For example, cleaning the group head, shower screen, portafilter, and filter basket removes coffee residue. Descaling focuses on mineral deposits inside the machine.

Read our guide on how to clean a Breville espresso machine for additional maintenance instructions.

What You Need Before Descaling a Breville Espresso Machine

Before starting, collect the necessary supplies. Having everything ready makes the process easier and reduces the possibility of interrupting the descaling cycle.

Essential Descaling Supplies

  1. Breville descaling solution: A manufacturer-approved product designed to dissolve mineral deposits.

  2. Breville descaling powder: An alternative descaling product when specified as compatible with your machine.

  3. Clean water: Fresh water for preparing the descaling solution mixture and completing the rinse cycle.

  4. Large container: A heat-resistant container to collect water and descaling solution from the machine.

  5. Clean cloth: Useful for wiping spills and cleaning the machine's exterior.

Choosing the Right Espresso Machine Descaler

The best descaling solution for Breville depends on your machine's instructions and the manufacturer's recommendations.

A suitable espresso machine descaler should be compatible with the internal materials and heating system of your appliance.

Consider these options:

  • Breville descaling solution: A convenient option when available for your particular machine.

  • Breville descaling powder: Follow the package instructions to dissolve descaling powder using the recommended quantity of water.

  • Compatible commercial descaler: Choose a product explicitly approved for your machine type.

Avoid mixing different descaling products. Never combine cleaning chemicals, and always follow the product's dilution instructions.

Can You Use Vinegar to Descale Breville?

Although vinegar is sometimes recommended as a household descaling option, it is generally not the best choice for Breville espresso machines.

Vinegar can leave a strong smell and taste, and its use may conflict with the manufacturer's maintenance instructions. It can also be unsuitable for certain internal materials and components.

Use a manufacturer-approved descaling product instead.

Can You Descale Breville With Citric Acid?

Citric acid is another substance used to dissolve mineral deposits in household appliances. However, that does not automatically make it suitable for every espresso machine.

Before using citric acid, check your specific Breville model's instructions. Using an unapproved concentration or product can create maintenance problems.

How to Descale a Breville Espresso Machine Step by Step

The general descaling process involves preparing the machine, adding the descaling product, activating the appropriate maintenance program, and flushing internal components.

However, different Breville machines use different button combinations and maintenance procedures. Always check the instruction manual for your exact model before entering descale mode.

Step 1: Turn Off the Machine and Prepare It

Start by switching off your Breville espresso machine and allowing it to cool if necessary.

Remove any coffee accessories that could interfere with the maintenance process.

Follow these preparation steps:

  1. Remove the portafilter from the group head.

  2. Empty the drip tray.

  3. Remove any coffee grounds from the filter basket.

  4. Empty the water reservoir.

  5. Remove the water filter if your model's descaling instructions require it.

  6. Check that the steam wand and hot water outlet are clear.

  7. Place a large container underneath the appropriate outlets.

Removing the water filter before descaling is important for models whose instructions specify this step. Descaling products should not be circulated through a filter unless the manufacturer explicitly permits it.

Step 2: Prepare the Descaling Solution Mixture

The next step is preparing the descaling solution mixture.

Depending on the product, you may need to mix a measured amount of liquid descaler or dissolve descaling powder in fresh water.

Follow the product's instructions carefully rather than guessing the concentration.

Important preparation tips:

  • Use the recommended quantity of descaling product.

  • Do not mix different descaling chemicals.

  • Avoid exceeding the maximum water tank capacity.

  • Use fresh water rather than leftover water from previous brewing sessions.

  • Make sure the solution is fully dissolved before filling the reservoir.

Step 3: Fill the Water Tank

Remove the water tank or water reservoir from the machine.

Pour the prepared descaling solution into the tank according to the instructions supplied with your machine and descaler.

Securely reinstall the reservoir and make sure it is correctly positioned.

If your model has a charcoal water filter, keep it removed during descaling when instructed by Breville. Replace or reinstall the filter according to its maintenance schedule after the process is complete.

Step 4: Enter Descaling Mode

The procedure for activating descale mode varies between Breville models.

Some machines use dedicated maintenance buttons, while others require a combination of buttons or menu selections.

For certain Barista Express versions, the maintenance instructions involve a specific button sequence. Do not assume that every model uses the same combination.

On models whose manual specifies it, you may need to hold 2 CUP and POWER buttons to activate the appropriate maintenance mode.

The machine may illuminate specific indicators or begin a maintenance sequence.

Step 5: Run the Descaling Cycle

Once the machine enters the correct maintenance program, allow the descaling cycle to begin.

The machine may release the solution through the group head, hot water outlet, and steam wand, depending on the model.

During this process:

  • Monitor the water level in the reservoir.

  • Keep the collection container correctly positioned.

  • Follow any instructions displayed on the machine.

  • Do not interrupt the cycle unnecessarily.

  • Never remove the reservoir while the machine is operating unless instructed.

The descaling solution gradually dissolves mineral deposits inside the water lines and other components reached by the maintenance program.

Step 6: Complete the Hot Water and Steam Functions

Some Breville machines require separate hot water and steam operations during descaling.

If your manual specifies these steps, operate the steam dial or hot water function as directed.

Allow the designated outlets to release the descaling solution into your collection container.

Do not force the steam dial or operate a function that is not part of your model's descaling instructions.

Step 7: Empty the Drip Tray and Water Tank

After the descaling solution has passed through the required components, empty the collection container and drip tray if instructed.

Remove the remaining solution from the water tank.

Rinse the reservoir thoroughly with fresh water to remove any remaining chemical residue.

Step 8: Perform a Fresh Water Rinse

The fresh water rinse is one of the most important parts of the process.

Fill the reservoir with clean water and follow the manufacturer's rinse instructions.

The rinse cycle helps flush internal components and remove any remaining descaling solution.

Depending on your model, you may need to run fresh water through the group head, hot water outlet, and steam wand.

Step 9: Reset the Descale Indicator

Some Breville machines automatically clear the maintenance notification after completing the correct cycle.

Others may require a separate reset procedure.

Follow your model's instructions to reset the descale indicator if necessary.

Once complete, reinstall the water filter if applicable and return the machine to normal operation.

How to Descale Different Breville Espresso Machine Models

Breville manufactures several espresso machine families, and their maintenance procedures are not identical.

The following sections explain the important differences between popular models.

How to Descale Breville Barista Express

The Breville Barista Express is one of the most popular home espresso machines.

The Barista Express BES870 combines a built-in grinder, espresso brewing system, and steam wand.

To descale this model:

  1. Remove the water filter if instructed.

  2. Empty the water tank and drip tray.

  3. Prepare the recommended descaling solution.

  4. Fill the reservoir according to the manual.

  5. Position a suitable container beneath the outlets.

  6. Activate the designated descale program.

  7. Follow the machine's instructions for the descaling and rinse stages.

  8. Reinstall the water filter when appropriate.

Important Barista Express Maintenance Details

The Barista Express has a dedicated cleaning and maintenance system. Its cleaning cycle and descaling cycle serve different purposes.

Do not confuse the cleaning tablet procedure with the descaling procedure.

When asking when to descale Breville Barista Express, consider your water hardness, machine usage, and the maintenance notification.

How to Descale Breville Barista Express Impress

The Barista Express Impress features an assisted tamping system and an integrated grinder.

Its descaling procedure should follow the dedicated instructions for the Impress model.

Pay particular attention to the water reservoir, maintenance indicators, and the correct sequence for activating the descaling program.

Do not assume that instructions for the original BES870 apply to every Impress version.

How to Descale Breville Barista Pro

The Barista Pro uses a thermocoil heating system and an LCD interface.

Its display helps guide users through different maintenance requirements.

To descale the Barista Pro:

  1. Check the machine's maintenance notification.

  2. Remove the water filter when instructed.

  3. Empty the reservoir and drip tray.

  4. Add the recommended descaling mixture.

  5. Follow the LCD instructions to start the maintenance program.

  6. Complete all required descaling and rinsing stages.

The display-based maintenance system makes it easier for beginners to follow the correct sequence.

How to Descale Breville Barista Touch

The Barista Touch includes a touchscreen interface that provides access to coffee preparation and maintenance functions.

Its descaling instructions are model-specific.

Open the maintenance menu and follow the displayed instructions for preparing the solution, operating the machine, and completing the rinse cycle.

Make sure the machine has finished all required stages before returning to normal espresso preparation.

How to Descale Breville Barista Touch Impress

The Barista Touch Impress combines touchscreen controls with assisted tamping and dosing features.

Its maintenance procedure should be performed using the instructions supplied for the Touch Impress rather than relying on the original Barista Touch procedure.

Follow the on-screen maintenance prompts and make sure the water reservoir contains the correct solution during the descaling stage.

How to Descale Breville Bambino

The Breville Bambino is a compact espresso machine designed for home coffee preparation.

Its descaling procedure differs from larger machines with dedicated LCD maintenance menus.

Consult the Bambino instruction manual for the exact button sequence and descaling instructions.

Pay particular attention to the water reservoir, steam wand, and hot water functions.

How to Descale Breville Bambino Plus

The Bambino Plus includes automatic milk texturing features and a compact heating system.

For effective maintenance:

  • Follow the Bambino Plus-specific descaling instructions.

  • Use a compatible descaling product.

  • Remove the water filter if required.

  • Complete the entire rinse procedure.

  • Check that the steam wand operates correctly afterward.

How to Descale Breville Oracle and Oracle Touch

The Breville Oracle and Oracle Touch are advanced espresso machines with automated coffee preparation features.

Their maintenance procedures may involve multiple internal systems and model-specific instructions.

Follow the maintenance menu or manufacturer's manual carefully.

Do not use a generic button combination from another Breville machine.

How to Descale Breville Dual Boiler

The Dual Boiler uses separate boilers for espresso brewing and steam production.

This makes its maintenance requirements different from single-heating-system machines.

Use the Dual Boiler-specific descaling instructions. Pay attention to the boiler maintenance requirements and any warnings about internal components.

If the machine shows persistent heating or water-flow problems, professional servicing may be necessary.

How Often Should You Descale a Breville Espresso Machine?

How often to descale Breville espresso machine depends primarily on water hardness, frequency of use, and the type of water filter installed.

If you live in an area with hard water, mineral buildup can develop more quickly. Homes using filtered or softer water may need descaling less frequently.

Recommended Descaling Frequency

Water conditions

Suggested maintenance approach

Soft water

Follow the machine's longer recommended maintenance interval

Moderately hard water

Monitor the descale alert and follow the manual

Hard water

Check for scale buildup more frequently

Heavy daily usage

Monitor water flow and maintenance notifications regularly

These are general guidelines rather than fixed manufacturer intervals.

Signs Your Breville Needs Descaling

Look for these common warning signs:

  • The Clean/Descale light illuminates or flashes.

  • The machine displays a descale alert.

  • Espresso flow becomes unusually slow.

  • Water takes longer to reach the correct brewing temperature.

  • The machine produces inconsistent espresso.

  • The steam wand produces less steam than usual.

  • The pump sounds different during operation.

  • Mineral deposits become visible around water outlets.

Should You Wait Until the Descale Light Comes On?

No. The maintenance indicator is useful, but you should also consider water quality and usage.

If you regularly use hard water, mineral deposits can accumulate before a notification appears.

How to Rinse a Breville Espresso Machine After Descaling

A proper rinse is essential because leftover descaling solution can affect the flavor of your next coffee.

Follow these steps to complete the rinse cycle safely.

Step 1: Empty the Remaining Descaling Solution

Remove the water tank and discard any remaining descaling mixture.

Rinse the reservoir thoroughly with clean water.

Step 2: Fill the Tank With Fresh Water

Fill the water reservoir with fresh drinking water.

Make sure the reservoir is correctly installed before operating the machine.

Step 3: Flush the Internal Components

Follow the machine's rinse instructions to flush the internal water system.

Depending on the model, this may involve:

  • Running water through the group head.

  • Operating the hot water outlet.

  • Flushing the steam wand.

  • Completing the automatic rinse cycle.

Step 4: Check the Water Quality

Once the rinse cycle is complete, check that the water has no unusual chemical smell or taste.

If necessary, perform another rinse according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Step 5: Reinstall the Water Filter

If you removed the charcoal water filter before descaling, reinstall it or replace it if it has reached the end of its service life.

Your Breville espresso machine should now be ready for normal operation.

Common Breville Descaling Problems and How to Fix Them

Sometimes the descaling process does not work as expected. Your machine may stop halfway through the maintenance program, fail to dispense water, or continue displaying the maintenance notification.

Here are common problems and their solutions.

Breville Descale Not Working

If your Breville descale not working problem continues, first check whether you are following the correct instructions for your specific model.

Possible causes include:

  • Incorrect descaling procedure.

  • Incomplete maintenance cycle.

  • Incorrect solution preparation.

  • Water reservoir not properly installed.

  • Blocked internal water passages.

  • Machine not detecting the maintenance sequence.

Solution: Restart the process only after checking the manufacturer's troubleshooting instructions. Avoid repeatedly running the machine without water.

Breville Descale Mode Not Starting

If Breville descale mode not starting, the button combination may be incorrect.

Different models have different maintenance activation procedures.

Try the following:

  1. Switch off the machine.

  2. Check the model number.

  3. Consult the appropriate instruction manual.

  4. Repeat the correct activation sequence.

  5. Check whether the maintenance indicator responds.

What About Holding 2 CUP and POWER Buttons?

Some Breville models use a combination involving the 2 CUP and POWER buttons for specific maintenance functions.

However, this is not a universal procedure. Only use this combination when the instructions for your particular model specify it.

Descaling Solution Not Flowing

If descaling solution not flowing through the machine, there may be a blockage or an issue with the water supply.

Check:

  • Whether the water tank contains enough solution.

  • Whether the reservoir is correctly positioned.

  • Whether the water outlet is obstructed.

  • Whether the machine has an existing water-flow problem.

Do not continue operating the pump if the machine is running dry.

Water Not Coming Out of Breville Espresso Machine

Water not coming out can indicate several issues, including a blocked water line, an improperly installed reservoir, or a pump problem.

Try these basic checks:

  1. Confirm that the reservoir contains enough water.

  2. Check that the tank is properly seated.

  3. Inspect the water filter for incorrect installation.

  4. Check the group head for visible obstructions.

  5. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for restoring water flow.

If the pump operates but no water comes out, professional inspection may be necessary.

Blocked Steam Wand

A blocked steam wand can result from dried milk residue or mineral deposits.

First, distinguish between a steam wand blockage caused by milk and one caused by internal scale buildup.

For external milk residue, use the recommended steam wand cleaning procedure.

For suspected internal mineral deposits, follow the model-specific descaling instructions.

Never insert sharp objects deep into the steam system.

Slow Espresso Flow

Slow espresso flow is not always caused by limescale.

Other possible causes include:

  • Coffee grounds that are too finely ground.

  • Excessive coffee dosage.

  • Over-tamping.

  • A clogged filter basket.

  • Dirty shower screen.

  • Mineral buildup in internal pipes.

If the machine has recently been descaled but espresso flow remains slow, check the coffee preparation variables and clean the brewing components.

Machine Not Pumping Water

If the machine not pumping water, check the reservoir, water filter, and power supply first.

A pump that cannot move water may indicate an obstruction or mechanical problem.

Do not repeatedly run the machine in an attempt to force water through a blockage.

Incomplete Descale Cycle

An incomplete descale cycle can occur if the water tank becomes empty, the machine loses power, or the maintenance process is interrupted.

Check your model's instructions to determine whether the cycle can be resumed or must be restarted.

Complete all required descaling and rinsing stages before preparing coffee.

Why Does My Breville Descale Light Stay On?

If the descale light stays on after maintenance, the machine may not have registered the complete descaling procedure.

Possible reasons include:

  • The maintenance cycle was interrupted.

  • The rinse cycle was not completed.

  • The wrong maintenance program was selected.

  • The indicator requires a separate reset procedure.

Follow the manufacturer's reset instructions rather than repeatedly performing unnecessary descaling cycles.

Why Is My Breville Descale Light Flashing?

A flashing descale indicator can mean that the machine requires maintenance or that a maintenance process has not been completed.

Its meaning depends on the model.

Check the user manual to identify the specific indicator pattern and the required action.

How to Remove Limescale From a Breville Espresso Machine Effectively

Removing limescale requires a compatible descaling product and the correct maintenance procedure.

Mineral deposits can accumulate in several internal areas, including:

  • Water lines.

  • Internal pipes.

  • Heating element.

  • Boiler.

  • Thermocoil.

  • Water outlets.

  • Other components exposed to heated water.

The descaling solution works by dissolving mineral deposits that the machine's maintenance program reaches.

Can You Remove All Scale With One Descaling Cycle?

Not necessarily.

The amount of mineral buildup, machine condition, and descaling procedure can affect the results.

A lightly scaled machine may respond to one complete maintenance cycle, while a machine with substantial deposits may require professional attention.

Do not run repeated chemical treatments without checking the manufacturer's recommendations.

How to Maintain a Breville Espresso Machine After Descaling

Descaling is only one part of maintaining your espresso machine.

Regular cleaning and good water management can help reduce mineral buildup and keep your equipment performing consistently.

Daily Maintenance

After preparing coffee:

  • Clean the portafilter and filter basket.

  • Wipe the group head.

  • Remove coffee residue from the shower screen.

  • Purge and wipe the steam wand according to the manual.

  • Empty and rinse the drip tray.

  • Wipe the exterior with a clean cloth.

Weekly Maintenance

Depending on your usage, perform these additional tasks:

  • Clean removable brewing accessories.

  • Inspect the shower screen.

  • Check the steam wand for milk residue.

  • Clean the water reservoir.

  • Inspect the drip tray and surrounding areas.

Monthly Maintenance

Check the condition of the water filter and review the machine's maintenance indicators.

The actual filter replacement schedule depends on the filter type and usage.

Use Suitable Water

Water hardness has a significant influence on mineral accumulation.

Using water within the hardness range recommended by Breville can help reduce scale formation.

A charcoal water filter may improve water quality, but it does not eliminate the need for descaling.

Follow a Consistent Cleaning Schedule

For more maintenance advice, see our guide on how to clean an espresso machine.

If you are new to espresso preparation, our guide to using an espresso machine also explains the basic brewing process and equipment.

Breville Cleaning Cycle vs. Descaling Cycle: What's the Difference?

One common mistake among beginners is confusing the cleaning cycle with the descaling cycle.

Although both help maintain the machine, they have different purposes.

When Should You Use Each Cycle?

Use the cleaning cycle when coffee oils and residue accumulate around the brewing system.

Use the descaling cycle when mineral deposits develop inside the water system.

Neither process replaces the other.

Frequently Asked Questions About Descaling Breville Espresso Machines

1. How Often Should I Descale My Breville Espresso Machine?

The frequency depends on water hardness, usage, and the specific machine. Follow the maintenance schedule in your Breville manual and monitor the descale indicator.

2. How Long Does It Take to Descale a Breville Espresso Machine?

The time varies by model and the number of maintenance stages. Allow enough time to complete the full descaling process, including the fresh water rinse. Check your model's manual for the expected duration.

3. What Is the Best Descaling Solution for Breville?

A Breville-approved descaling product is a suitable choice. You can also consider another product explicitly compatible with your particular machine.

4. Can You Use Vinegar to Descale Breville?

Vinegar is generally not recommended as a substitute for an approved descaling product. It can leave an unpleasant smell and may not be suitable for your machine.

5. Can You Descale Breville With Citric Acid?

Citric acid can dissolve mineral deposits, but you should only use it if your particular machine's manufacturer instructions permit it.

6. How Do I Descale Breville Without a Water Filter?

You can generally descale a Breville machine without an installed water filter, provided you follow the model-specific instructions.

If your machine normally uses a filter, remove it before descaling when directed by the manufacturer.

7. Does Descaling Improve Espresso Taste?

Descaling can improve coffee consistency when mineral buildup has been affecting water flow or brewing temperature.

It does not directly improve coffee bean quality, grinder performance, or extraction variables.

8. What Happens If I Never Descale My Breville?

Mineral deposits can gradually accumulate inside the machine, potentially restricting water flow, affecting heating performance, and increasing the risk of equipment problems.

9. Should I Remove the Water Filter Before Descaling?

For many Breville models, the instructions require removing the filter before descaling. Always check the exact procedure for your model.

10. Can I Make Coffee Immediately After Descaling?

Yes, once the complete descaling and rinsing procedures have finished. Make sure there is no remaining descaling solution in the water system.

11. Why Is My Breville Still Showing a Descale Alert?

The machine may not have registered the complete maintenance cycle, or it may require a separate indicator reset. Follow the relevant manual.

12. Can I Use Regular Tap Water After Descaling?

You can use tap water if its hardness and mineral content meet the manufacturer's recommendations. Filtered water may be a suitable alternative.

13. Does Descaling Damage an Espresso Machine?

Using the correct product and following the manufacturer's procedure should help protect the machine. Incorrect chemicals, concentrations, or maintenance procedures can create problems.

14. Is Descaling the Same as Backflushing?

No. Backflushing cleans the brewing system using an appropriate cleaning process, while descaling removes mineral deposits from the internal water system.

15. How Do I Know When My Breville Needs Descaling?

Check the maintenance indicator, water flow, and machine performance. Hard water and frequent use can increase the need for maintenance.

Final Thoughts

Learning how to descale a Breville espresso machine is an important part of maintaining your home coffee equipment. Regular descaling helps remove mineral buildup, supports consistent water flow, and protects internal components from excessive scale accumulation.

Whether you use a Breville Barista Express, Barista Pro, Bambino Plus, Barista Touch, or Oracle, always follow the maintenance instructions for your exact model. Use a compatible descaling product, complete the entire rinse cycle, and monitor water quality to reduce future mineral buildup.

With proper cleaning, suitable water, and consistent maintenance, your Breville espresso machine can continue producing enjoyable espresso for years.
